subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Generosity Principle
description: A quick, practical guide to The Generosity Principle.

hook.text: Adam Grant studied professionals who give without keeping score. They consistently outperform selfish networkers.

buildup.text: Givers introduce contacts, share resources, and offer help freely. It seems like a losing strategy short-term.

discovery.text: Generosity creates reciprocity over time. People remember who helped them and return the favor unprompted.

twist.text: Givers must set boundaries. Helping everyone at your own expense leads to burnout, not a strong network.

climax.text: Be a strategic giver: help freely, but protect your time. Five-minute favors — quick intros, brief advice — cost little.

punchline.text: Give five-minute favors freely. The returns compound.

quiz.question: What's the key to being a successful 'giver' in networking?
options: Help everyone with everything, regardless of time cost
Be a strategic giver: help freely with small favors while protecting your time
Keep a detailed record of every favor given and received
